key_insight: PMA addresses a neglected failure mode in continual multimodal instruction tuning: the projector can forget past visual-language alignment, so it is progressively expanded while keeping the original projector as a stable anchor.
engineering_relevance: For multimodal systems used in engineering workflows, PMA offers a practical way to update models over time without sacrificing earlier alignment, improving robustness under shifting data and tasks.
method: Detect multimodal distribution shifts with a lightweight representation descriptor.
Expand projector experts only when drift is detected, rather than retraining the whole alignment module.
Use an expandable router to combine expert outputs while retaining the pretrained projector as an anchor.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent gains over prior state of the art on two recent MCIT benchmarks and good transfer across multiple MLLM backbones.
watch_item: Because PMA adds experts progressively, deployment must manage router reliability and the extra parameter/latency overhead as the system grows.
paper_title: Progressive Multimodal Alignment for Continual Instruction Tuning
